name: en-public
description: PRD §7.1 EN-Public: 30 English Wikipedia articles in three clusters with deliberate near-duplicate facts (data-protection law, space missions, bridges) plus 120 arXiv abstracts (conformal prediction, RAG, hallucination detection, NLI, selective prediction). Queries were drafted by Claude (Anthropic) from the corpus with verbatim evidence checked mechanically, and are status=draft until verified by a person (python -m aletheia.eval.review). Unanswerable queries are near-miss traps whose answer is absent from this corpus snapshot. Sources and licences: SOURCES.md.

queries.text: From what date did the EU's GDPR actually start to apply?
evidence: adopted the GDPR on 14 April 2016, to become effective on 25 May 2018
queries.note: Distractor: adoption date 14 April 2016 in the same sentence; UK DPA 2018 also came into effect 25 May 2018 (different law).

queries.text: How many explanatory recitals accompany the articles of the GDPR?
evidence: The GDPR also contains 173 recitals purposed to clarify scope and rationale
queries.note: Easy numeric lookup; 'eleven chapters' in the preceding sentence is a nearby distractor.

queries.text: Into how many chapters is the GDPR organised?
evidence: The GDPR 2016 has eleven chapters
queries.note: Distractor: 173 recitals in the next sentence; DPA 2018 has seven parts; LGPD has 65 articles.

queries.text: Under the GDPR, what is the maximum fine for breaching a controller's obligations under Articles 25 to 39, such as data protection by design?
evidence: a fine up to €10 million or up to 2% of the annual worldwide turnover of the preceding financial year in case of an enterprise, whichever is greater, if there has been an infringement of the following provisions (Article 83, Paragraph 4)
queries.answer: Up to €10 million or 2% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is greater
queries.note: Hard: two fine tiers in the GDPR (€10m/2% vs €20m/4%) plus LGPD's 2%/R$50m and CCPA's $7,500; the question targets the lower tier via the Articles 25-39 list.

queries.text: What is the GDPR's top-tier fine for infringing data subjects' rights under Articles 12 to 22?
evidence: a fine up to €20 million or up to 4% of the annual worldwide turnover of the preceding financial year in case of an enterprise, whichever is greater, if there has been an infringement of the following provisions (Article 83, Paragraph 5 & 6)
queries.answer: Up to €20 million or 4% of annual worldwide turnover, whichever is greater
queries.note: Distractor: the €10m/2% tier just above; LGPD 2% cap; Schrems' 4% preliminary order against Facebook.

queries.text: How long does a controller have under the GDPR to report a personal data breach to the supervisory authority after becoming aware of it?
evidence: There is a maximum of 72 hours after becoming aware of the data breach to make the report.
queries.note: Distractors: LGPD sets no fixed period ('reasonable time'); HIPAA's 30-day access deadline; PIPL has no deadline stated.

queries.text: Below what age does the GDPR require parental consent for a child's data processing, and how low can member states set it?
evidence: Consent for children, defined in the regulation as being less than 16 years old (although with the option for member states to individually make it as low as 13 years old)
queries.answer: Under 16, lowerable by member states to 13
queries.note: Near-duplicate facts: CCPA uses 13 and 13–16; PIPL treats under-14s' data as sensitive.

queries.text: Above what headcount must an organisation keep records of processing activities under Article 30 of the GDPR?
evidence: employing more than 250 people;
queries.note: Short list item; retriever must match 'records of processing activities'. Only one of several alternative criteria.

queries.text: Which GDPR article obliges non-EU establishments to designate an EU Representative?
evidence: Under Article 27, non-EU establishments subject to GDPR are obliged to have a designee within the European Union
queries.note: Distractors: Article 37 (DPO), Article 3(2) (territorial scope) in nearby passages; PIPL also requires a representative in China.

queries.text: Until what date did the European Commission renew its adequacy decision for the UK in December 2025?
evidence: On 19 December 2025 the Commission renewed the 2021 adequacy decision until 27 December 2031.
queries.note: Distractors: original expiry 27 June 2025, six-month extension, 28 June 2021 adoption; question needs the renewal end date.

queries.text: When did the EDPB officially recognise the Europrivacy criteria as a European Data Protection Seal?
evidence: In October 2022, the Europrivacy certification criteria were officially recognized by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) to serve as European Data Protection Seal.
queries.note: Distractor: October 2022 also appears in the Privacy Shield file (Biden executive order, 7 October 2022).

queries.text: What was the estimated total cost of GDPR compliance for US companies?
evidence: The total cost for EU companies is estimated at €200 billion while for US companies the estimate is for $41.7 billion.
queries.note: Must pick the US figure, not the EU €200 billion in the same sentence, nor the US$100,000 per-company spending figure.

queries.text: In which CJEU case did the court interpret the GDPR right to compensation, holding that the damage need not reach a certain degree of seriousness?
evidence: In the judgment Österreichische Post (C-300/21) the Court of Justice of the European Union gave an interpretation of the right to compensation.
queries.note: Name/case-number lookup; diacritics may trip lexical matching. Google Spain (right to erasure) is a nearby distractor case.

queries.text: On what date did President Clinton sign HIPAA into law?
evidence: signed into law by President Bill Clinton on August 21, 1996
queries.note: Easy; distractor dates for later HIPAA rules (2003, 2006, 2013).

queries.text: Under HIPAA Title I, how long a gap without creditable coverage counts as a 'significant break'?
evidence: A "significant break" in coverage is defined as any 63-day period without any creditable coverage.
queries.note: Distractors: 12- and 18-month exclusion periods in the same paragraph.

queries.text: For how long can a group health plan exclude pre-existing conditions for someone who enrolls late, under HIPAA?
evidence: Group health plans may refuse to provide benefits in relation to preexisting conditions for either 12 months following enrollment in the plan or 18 months in the case of late enrollment.
queries.note: Must choose 18 (late enrollment) over 12 (normal enrollment); '18 months' also appears for continuous coverage.

queries.text: When did the HIPAA Privacy Rule come into effect?
evidence: The Privacy Rule came into effect on April 14, 2003, with a one-year extension for certain "small plans".
queries.note: Tricky near-duplicate: GDPR adopted 14 April 2016 (same day/month); Security Rule issued February 20, 2003; EDI rule October 16, 2003.

queries.text: How many days does a provider have to give a patient a copy of their health information after a written request under HIPAA?
evidence: After an individual requests information in writing (typically using the provider's form for this purpose), a provider has up to 30 days to provide a copy of the information to the individual.
queries.note: Also stated in the Privacy Rule paragraph ('within 30 days'). Distractor: GDPR 72-hour breach deadline.

queries.text: After the 2013 Omnibus Rule, for how long after a person's death is their PHI protected?
evidence: Protection of PHI was changed from indefinite to 50 years after death.
queries.note: Easy single fact; paraphrase avoids 'Omnibus' matching trivially only if retriever relies on it.

queries.text: How many digits does a HIPAA National Provider Identifier have?
evidence: The NPI is 10 digits (may be alphanumeric), with the last digit being a checksum.
queries.note: Easy numeric; question uses the expanded name, passage uses 'NPI'.

queries.text: When did the HIPAA Enforcement Rule become effective?
evidence: It became effective on March 16, 2006.
queries.note: Distractor: issued February 16, 2006 in the previous sentence.

queries.text: How much was Hospice of North Idaho fined in the first HIPAA Security Rule case involving fewer than 500 people?
evidence: This may have changed with the fining of $50,000 to the Hospice of North Idaho (HONI)
queries.note: Distractors: UCLA $865,500 settlement, $5.5m and $4.3m largest fines; 441 patient records.

queries.text: Which organisation received the largest HIPAA fine listed, and how much was it?
evidence: The largest fines of $5.5 million, levied against Memorial Healthcare Systems in 2017
queries.note: Distractor: $4.3 million against Cignet Health (2010) in same sentence; Tricare largest data loss.

queries.text: Between April 2003 and January 2013, how many HIPAA complaints did OCR receive and how many were referred to the Justice Department?
evidence: it received 91,000 complaints of HIPAA violations, in which 22,000 led to enforcement actions of varying kinds (from settlements to fines) and 521 led to referrals to the U.S. Department of Justice
queries.note: Many competing counts: 23,886 complaints (2003-2006), 19,306 resolved cases, 9,146 and 44,118 case counts.

queries.text: In the University of Michigan study, how far did completion of follow-up surveys for heart-attack patients drop after the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
evidence: resulted in a drop from 96% to 34% in the proportion of follow-up surveys completed by study patients being followed after a heart attack
queries.note: Distractor: 73% decrease in patient accrual in the cancer-prevention study (next sentence).

queries.text: When did China's Personal Information Protection Law take effect?
evidence: The PIPL was adopted on August 20, 2021, and is effective November 1, 2021.
queries.note: Distractors: adoption date August 20, 2021; reference English version December 29, 2021.

queries.text: Under the PIPL, up to what age is all of a minor's personal information treated as sensitive?
evidence: All personal information of minors under the age of 14 is sensitive
queries.note: Near-duplicate child-age facts: GDPR 16 (down to 13), CCPA 13 and 13-16.

queries.text: Which GDPR lawful basis has no equivalent in China's PIPL?
evidence: Unlike in the GDPR, there is no legitimate interests basis.
queries.note: Stated twice in the PIPL file; LGPD by contrast includes legitimate interest.

queries.text: Which PIPL article requires separate consent for cross-border transfers of personal data?
evidence: Cross-border transfers of personal data (Article 39).
queries.note: List of separate-consent articles (23, 25, 26, 29, 39); Article 40 (security assessment/large processors) is a near-miss.

queries.text: When was a reference English translation of the PIPL published?
evidence: A reference English version was published on December 29, 2021.
queries.note: Distractor: adoption and effective dates in preceding sentence.

queries.text: Which PIPL article requires separate consent for processing sensitive personal data?
evidence: Processing of sensitive personal data (Article 29); and
queries.note: Must choose 29 among 23/25/26/29/39 in the same list.

queries.text: Since when have China's Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows been in effect?
evidence: In March 2024, the Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows, which CAC had issued, became effective.
queries.note: Only date in the overseas-transfers section; question paraphrases 'became effective'.

queries.text: What must foreign companies covered by the PIPL's long-arm provisions set up in China?
evidence: All such entities are required to establish a dedicated entity or appoint a representative within China.
queries.answer: A dedicated entity or an appointed representative within China
queries.note: Analogous to GDPR Article 27 EU Representative (distractor in GDPR file).

queries.text: In what year was privacy activist Max Schrems born?
evidence: Maximilian Schrems (born 1987) is an Austrian activist
queries.note: Easy; many other years (2011-2021) in the article.

queries.text: How many pages of personal data did Facebook send Schrems after his access request?
evidence: received a CD containing over 1,200 pages of data
queries.note: Single number; paraphrase of 'Right of access'.

queries.text: At which US university was Schrems on a semester abroad when he began writing about Facebook and EU privacy law?
evidence: While studying law during a semester abroad at Santa Clara University in Silicon Valley
queries.note: Easy; see unanswerable item on his home university (not in corpus).

queries.text: How many Facebook users were allowed to join Schrems' 2014 Austrian class action, and how much did he claim per participant?
evidence: Within six days the participation in the suit was limited to 25,000 Facebook users
for a "token amount" of €500 in damages per participant
queries.note: Two numbers in adjacent sentences; distractor 20 of 22 claims, EUR 500 token judgment.

queries.text: On what date did the CJEU invalidate the Safe Harbor framework in Schrems I?
evidence: On 6 October 2015, the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that
(2) the Safe Harbor framework is invalid
queries.note: Distractors: AG Bot opinion 23 September 2015, hearing 24 March 2015; Privacy Shield file only says 'October 2015'. The 'Safe Harbor is invalid' part is later in the same sentence.

queries.text: Who was the Advocate General in Schrems I and when did he deliver his opinion?
evidence: The court's Advocate General for the case was Yves Bot.
Bot delivered his opinion on 23 September 2015.
queries.note: Name and date in separate sentences; date distractor 6 October 2015 (judgment).

queries.text: What was the total value of the three GDPR complaints Schrems filed against Google and Facebook in 2018?
evidence: Three complaints totalling over €3.9 billion were filed.
queries.note: Distractor: €18.8 billion predicted for 8 companies in 2019 complaints.

queries.text: Which litigation funder financed Schrems' Vienna class action against Facebook?
evidence: The case was financed by the German litigation funder ROLAND ProzessFinanz.
queries.note: Name lookup; paraphrased.

queries.text: Which Irish High Court judge adjourned Schrems' case pending a CJEU reference in June 2014?
evidence: On 18 June 2014, Mr. Justice Hogan adjourned the case pending a reference to the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU).
queries.note: Distractors: Ms Justice Costello (2017 referral), Mr Justice David Barniville (2021).

queries.text: When did the California Consumer Privacy Act take effect?
evidence: The CCPA became effective on January 1, 2020.
queries.note: Distractors: signed June 28, 2018; amendments September 13, 2018 and October 11, 2019; Prop 24 November 2020.

queries.text: Which governor signed the CCPA, and on what date?
evidence: signed into law by the Governor of California, Jerry Brown, on June 28, 2018
queries.note: Distractor: Gov. Newsom signed 2019 amendments.

queries.text: What annual gross revenue threshold brings a business under the CCPA?
evidence: Has annual gross revenues in excess of $25 million in its most recent tax year;
queries.note: One of three alternative thresholds; others are 100,000 consumers and >50% revenue from selling data.

queries.text: How many consumers' or households' personal information must a business buy, receive or sell to fall under the CCPA?
evidence: Buys, receives, or sells the personal information of 100,000 or more consumers or households; or
queries.note: Distractor: $25 million threshold; GDPR's US$100,000 spending figure.

queries.text: What statutory damages range can courts award per California resident per incident after a data breach under the CCPA?
evidence: pay statutory damages between $100 and $750 per California resident and incident, or actual damages, whichever is greater
queries.note: Distractor: $7,500 / $2,500 civil fines in the next item.

queries.text: What is the CCPA fine for each intentional violation?
evidence: A fine up to $7,500 for each intentional violation and $2,500 for each unintentional violation
queries.note: Must pick intentional figure; statutory damages $100-$750 nearby.

queries.text: Under the CCPA, how long must a business wait before asking a consumer who opted out to opt back in?
evidence: Avoid requesting opt-in consent for 12 months after a California resident opts out
queries.note: Only duration in CCPA file; paraphrased.

queries.text: Which agency did California's Proposition 24 create?
evidence: establishing the California Privacy Protection Agency
queries.note: Proposition 24 = California Privacy Rights Act; retrieval must link the proposition number to the history paragraph.

queries.text: When did Canada's PIPEDA become law?
evidence: PIPEDA became law on 13 April 2000 to promote consumer trust in electronic commerce.
queries.note: Distractors: staged implementation 2001/2002/2004; HIPAA Privacy Rule April 14, 2003.

queries.text: How often must Parliament review Part I of PIPEDA, and when was the first review?
evidence: must be reviewed by Parliament every five years. The first Parliamentary review occurred in 2007.
queries.note: Two-part answer from adjacent sentences.

queries.text: In what year was the Canadian Standards Association's Model Code, incorporated into PIPEDA, developed?
evidence: Canadian Standards Association's Model Code for the Protection of Personal Information, developed in 1995
queries.note: Distractor: 95/46/EC Data Protection Directive in GDPR file is also from 1995.

queries.text: In which year was PIPEDA extended to cover the health sector?
evidence: In 2002, the law was expanded to include the health sector.
queries.note: Distractors: 2001 federally regulated industries, 2004 all commercial activity; PHIPA established 2004.

queries.text: When did the Digital Privacy Act, which added mandatory breach notification to PIPEDA, become law?
evidence: On June 18, 2015, the Digital Privacy Act (Senate Bill S-4) became law
queries.note: Single date; question avoids 'Bill S-4'.

queries.text: In which 2024 case did Canada's Supreme Court find a reasonable expectation of privacy in IP addresses?
evidence: In R. v. Bykovets (2024), the Supreme Court of Canada ruled that individuals have a reasonable expectation of privacy in their IP addresses
queries.note: Name lookup; CCPA also lists IP addresses as personal information (distractor).

queries.text: Who proposed Bill C-475 to amend PIPEDA, and when was it defeated?
evidence: Bill C-475 was proposed in February 2013 by Charmaine Borg, MP, proposing several amendments to the Act.  Bill C-475 was defeated in January 2014.
queries.note: Two facts in adjacent sentences; February 2013 proposal date is a distractor for 'when'.

queries.text: On what date did the EU–US Privacy Shield go into effect?
evidence: The European Commission adopted the framework on 12 July 2016 and it went into effect the same day.
queries.note: Distractors: 8 July 2016 committee approval, 2 February 2016 political agreement, 16 July 2020 invalidation.

queries.text: When did the European Commission and the US government reach political agreement on the Privacy Shield?
evidence: on February 2, 2016, they reached a political agreement
queries.note: Distractors: several 2016 dates (April 13, May 30, July 8, July 12).

queries.text: When did the Article 29 Working Party issue its opinion on the Privacy Shield, and how many major concerns did it list?
evidence: The Article 29 Data Protection Working Party delivered an opinion on April 13, 2016, stating that the Privacy Shield offers major improvements compared to the Safe Harbor decisions, but that three major points of concern still remain.
queries.note: Distractor: EDPS opinion 30 May 2016.

queries.text: When did the European Data Protection Supervisor say the Privacy Shield was not robust enough to withstand future court scrutiny?
evidence: The European Data Protection Supervisor issued an opinion on 30 May 2016
queries.note: Distractor: Article 29 WP opinion April 13, 2016.

queries.text: What was the title of Trump's January 2017 executive order that excluded non-US persons from Privacy Act protections, and when was it repealed?
evidence: U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order entitled "Enhancing Public Safety"
This executive order was repealed by President Joe Biden on January 20, 2021.
queries.answer: "Enhancing Public Safety"; repealed January 20, 2021 by Biden
queries.note: Two-part; repeal date in a separate sentence. Distractor: Biden's 7 October 2022 order.

queries.text: When did the EU–US Umbrella Agreement enter into force?
evidence: The EU–US Umbrella Agreement, which enters into force on 1 February (2017).
queries.note: Distractor: January 25, 2017 executive order; Judicial Redress Act.

queries.text: When did Biden sign the executive order implementing the Trans-Atlantic Data Privacy Framework?
evidence: On 7 October 2022 President Biden signed an executive order to implement the European Union-U.S. data transfer framework
queries.note: Distractors: 25 March 2022 announcement; January 20, 2021 repeal; Europrivacy October 2022 in GDPR file.

queries.text: What is the official number of the ePrivacy Directive, and which directive amended it to require prior consent for cookies?
evidence: Privacy and Electronic Communications Directive 2002/58/EC on Privacy and Electronic Communications
This Directive has been amended by Directive 2009/136, which introduces several changes, especially in what concerns cookies, that are now subject to prior consent.
queries.note: Directive number 2002/58/EC in the opening sentence; Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC is a distractor.

queries.text: Which article of the ePrivacy Directive governs cookies?
evidence: The Directive provision applicable to cookies is Article 5(3).
queries.note: Distractors: Recitals 24/25, Article 13 (spam), Article 9 (location).

queries.text: Roughly how many hours a year do Europeans spend clicking through cookie consent banners?
evidence: Europeans collectively lose approximately 575 million hours each year clicking through cookie consent banners mandated by EU law.
queries.note: Easy numeric lookup.

queries.text: Unlike the Data Protection Directive, does the ePrivacy Directive also protect legal persons, and where is this stated?
evidence: Article 1(2) makes it clear that ePrivacy Directive also applies to legal persons.
queries.note: Tests contrast with DPD, which addresses only individuals.

queries.text: Which ePrivacy Directive article sets the opt-in rule for unsolicited marketing emails and SMS?
evidence: Article 13 prohibits the use of email addresses for marketing purposes.
queries.note: Distractor: Article 5(3) cookies, Article 15 exceptions.

queries.text: What is the maximum fine for breaching Brazil's LGPD?
evidence: Article 52 states that the maximum fine for breaching LGPD is two percent of a private company's revenue in Brazil, up to a maximum of 50 million reais.
queries.answer: 2% of the company's revenue in Brazil, capped at 50 million reais
queries.note: Near-duplicate: GDPR €10m/2% tier also uses 2%; answer must specify reais cap and Brazil revenue base.

queries.text: How many articles does the LGPD contain?
evidence: The LGPD contains sixty-five articles
queries.note: Distractor: 40 laws unified; GDPR 11 chapters / 173 recitals.

queries.text: From what date was the LGPD's enforceability backdated?
evidence: The LGPD became law on September 18, 2020, but its enforceability was backdated August 16, 2020.
queries.note: Many near dates: Sept 16/17/18 2020, Aug 14 2018, Aug 26 2020.

queries.text: From when could sanctions under the LGPD be applied?
evidence: Sanctions under the regulation will only be applied from August 1, 2021.
queries.note: Distractor: postponed effective date May 3, 2021 (MP 959).

queries.text: Which provisional measure created Brazil's national data protection authority, and who issued it?
evidence: On December 28, 2018 Michel Temer issued provisional measure 869
queries.answer: Provisional measure 869, issued by Michel Temer on December 28, 2018
queries.note: Distractor: Provisional Measure 959 by Bolsonaro.

queries.text: To what date did Provisional Measure 959 try to postpone the LGPD's effective date?
evidence: issued Provisional Measure 959 that postponed the effective date of the LGPD to May 3, 2021
queries.note: Distractor: Chamber of Deputies amended to December 31, 2020; Senate declared postponement void.

queries.text: Who introduced the Data Protection Bill to the House of Lords, and when?
evidence: The Data Protection Bill was introduced to the House of Lords by Lord Ashton of Hyde, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State at the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport on 13 September 2017.
queries.note: Distractors: royal assent 23 May 2018, in force 25 May 2018.

queries.text: How many parts does the UK Data Protection Act 2018 have?
evidence: The act has seven parts.
queries.note: Distractor: GDPR eleven chapters; Privacy Shield seven principles.

queries.text: Which part of the Data Protection Act 2018 deals with processing by the intelligence services?
evidence: Part 4 makes provision about the processing of personal data by the intelligence services.
queries.note: Distractor: Part 3 law enforcement, Part 5 Information Commissioner.

queries.text: On what date was the Data Protection Act 2018 amended to reflect the UK's status outside the EU?
evidence: It was amended on 1 January 2021 by regulations under the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018
queries.note: Distractors: 31 January 2020 withdrawal and 31 December 2020 transition end in GDPR file.

queries.text: Under which section of the Data Protection Act 2018 can a tribunal order the Information Commissioner to investigate?
evidence: in the tribunal by ordering the Information Commissioner to conduct an investigation (section 166)
queries.note: Distractors: section 167 compliance orders, section 162 appeals against penalty notices.

queries.text: Compare the headline maximum fines under the GDPR and Brazil's LGPD.
evidence: In some cases, violators of the GDPR may be fined up to €20 million or up to 4% of the annual worldwide turnover of the preceding financial year in case of an enterprise, whichever is greater.
the maximum fine for breaching LGPD is two percent of a private company's revenue in Brazil, up to a maximum of 50 million reais
queries.answer: GDPR: up to €20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover (whichever is greater); LGPD: 2% of revenue in Brazil capped at 50 million reais
queries.note: Needs both files; GDPR lower tier €10m/2% is a distractor that shares LGPD's 2%.

queries.text: The GDPR gives controllers a fixed deadline to report data breaches; what is it, and does the LGPD set a comparable fixed period?
evidence: There is a maximum of 72 hours after becoming aware of the data breach to make the report.
the LGPD does not specify a time period in which data breaches must be reported
queries.answer: GDPR: 72 hours; LGPD: no fixed period (a reasonable time as defined by ANPD)
queries.note: LGPD file alone states only that there's no period; the 72 hours comes from GDPR.

queries.text: At what age thresholds do the GDPR and China's PIPL give children's data special protection?
evidence: Consent for children, defined in the regulation as being less than 16 years old
All personal information of minors under the age of 14 is sensitive
queries.answer: GDPR: under 16 (member states may lower to 13); PIPL: under 14
queries.note: CCPA's 13/16 thresholds are a third distractor.

queries.text: Which took effect first, California's CCPA or the date to which Brazil's LGPD enforceability was backdated?
evidence: The CCPA became effective on January 1, 2020.
its enforceability was backdated August 16, 2020
queries.answer: The CCPA (January 1, 2020); the LGPD was backdated to August 16, 2020
queries.note: Comparison of two dates in different files; LGPD's many 2020 dates are distractors.

queries.text: How long after the CJEU struck down Safe Harbor did the EU–US Privacy Shield go into effect?
evidence: On 6 October 2015, the Court of Justice of the European Union ruled that
The EU–US Privacy Shield went into effect on 12 July 2016 following its approval by the European Commission.
queries.answer: About nine months: Safe Harbor invalidated 6 October 2015; Privacy Shield in effect 12 July 2016
queries.note: Privacy Shield file gives only 'October 2015' for Schrems I; exact day comes from Schrems file.

queries.text: Health data exempt from the CCPA falls under another US law instead; under that law, how many days does a provider have to give a patient a copy of their records?
evidence: it is expected for PHI to adhere to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, otherwise known as HIPAA
a provider has up to 30 days to provide a copy of the information to the individual
queries.note: Bridge question: CCPA exemption points to HIPAA; the 30-day rule is only in the HIPAA file.

queries.text: Can a controller rely on legitimate interests as a legal basis under Brazil's LGPD and under China's PIPL?
evidence: For the legitimate interest of the data controller or a third party, unless that would infringe upon the data subject's statutory rights.
Unlike in the GDPR, there is no legitimate interests basis.
queries.answer: LGPD: yes; PIPL: no, it has no legitimate interests basis
queries.note: GDPR's Article 6(1)(f) is a third-file distractor.

queries.text: Did the UK Data Protection Act 2018 come into effect on the same day the GDPR became applicable?
evidence: to become effective on 25 May 2018
The Act came into effect on 25 May 2018.
queries.note: Distractor: DPA royal assent 23 May 2018 appears in both files.

queries.text: How do the GDPR and the CCPA differ in the ages at which a child's data processing needs a parent's consent?
evidence: Consent for children, defined in the regulation as being less than 16 years old (although with the option for member states to individually make it as low as 13 years old), must be given by the child's parent or custodian
obtain parental or guardian consent for minors under 13 years and the affirmative consent of minors between 13 and 16 years
queries.answer: GDPR: parental consent under 16 (member states may lower to 13); CCPA: parental consent under 13, and the minor's own affirmative consent for ages 13-16
queries.note: Both laws use 13 and 16 but differently; easy to conflate.

queries.text: The Austrian campaigner who predicted a 'round-trip to Luxembourg' for the Privacy Shield — how old was he, roughly, when the Privacy Shield took effect?
evidence: Austrian campaigner Max Schrems criticized the new ruling, with the latter predicting that the commission might be taking a "round-trip to Luxembourg"
Maximilian Schrems (born 1987)
queries.answer: Max Schrems, born 1987, so about 28–29 in July 2016
queries.note: Multi-hop: identity from Privacy Shield file, birth year from Schrems file, arithmetic with 12 July 2016 (also in Privacy Shield file).

queries.text: What is the maximum fine, in yuan or as a share of turnover, for serious violations of China's PIPL?
queries.note: Retriever will hit the PIPL 'Enforcement – Severe penalties for violations' line and GDPR/LGPD fine passages; the PIPL file never states any fine amount (grep yuan/5%/renminbi: none).

queries.text: What is the annual cap on HIPAA civil money penalties for identical violations?
queries.note: HIPAA file ends with 'The differences between civil and criminal penalties are summarized in the following table:' but the table is missing; Enforcement Rule passage says it 'sets civil money penalties' without amounts. Distractors: $50,000 HONI, $5.5m largest fine.

queries.text: How many days does a business have to respond to a verifiable consumer request under the CCPA?
queries.note: CCPA file mentions access-request methods (toll-free number) and a 12-month opt-in wait, but no response deadline (no 'days' in the file). Distractor: HIPAA's 30-day access deadline.

queries.text: How large was the fine the Irish Data Protection Commission imposed on Meta in 2023 over EU–US data transfers?
